name: Zahmer Kaiser & Kaisertal
kurzbeschreibung: The Zahme Kaiser, with its gentle peaks and vast alpine meadows, is an ideal hiking area for families and food-loving walkers.
preis: Kostenlos (Parkplatz Kaisertal Sparchen ca. 5–6 € pro Tag)
beschreibung:
Overview

The Zahmer Kaiser constitutes the northern, greener, yet impressively rugged crest of the famous Kaisergebirge range in Tyrol. Stretching gracefully between Kufstein, Ebbs, Niederndorf, and Walchsee in the Kaiserwinkl, it rises north of the deeply carved, vehicle-free Kaisertal valley. The highest points are the Vordere Kesselschneid (2,002 m) and the distinctive Pyramidenspitze (1,997 m). In contrast to the stark limestone towers of the adjacent Wilder Kaiser, the Zahmer Kaiser showcases sweeping alpine forests, high-pasture meadows, steep grass couloirs, and mysterious karst caves. Chief among these is the legendary Tischofer Cave (Tischofer Höhle) in lower Kaisertal: excavations within this colossal cavern unearthed stone-age bones from over 400 cave bears, alongside prehistoric flint tools and Bronze Age human remains. Sheltered within the Kaisergebirge Nature Reserve, the range represents an idyllic haven of peace, rich alpine biodiversity, and heritage mountain guesthouses.

Route & Requirements

Trails spanning the Zahmer Kaiser accommodate both curious day strollers and endurance ridge summiters. The classic approach begins at Kufstein-Sparchen via the scenic Kaiseraufstieg staircase: ascending 280 stone steps, visitors access the tranquil valley trail leading gently to the marked branch for Tischofer Cave. The descent into the cave follows a secured woodland path (approx. 1 to 1.5 hours walk from trailhead, easy-to-moderate grade T1/T2, a thrill for surefooted children). Further inside the Kaisertal, hikers discover the historic Anton-Karg-Haus (Hinterbärenbad, 829 m) and Hans-Berger-Haus. True mountaineers set out from Durchholzen at Walchsee, climbing past Aschinger Alm and up the Winkelkar cirque to the summit of Pyramidenspitze (3.5 to 4 hours, 1,300 vertical meters gain, grade T3, requiring surefootedness on scree). Sturdy trekking footwear and headlamps for cave inspection are recommended. Leashed dogs are permitted on all valley and mountain trails.

Visit & Arrival

Arriving by rail is seamless via mainline ÖBB trains to Kufstein main station. From the station forecourt, local Kufstein city bus lines 1 or 2 deliver passengers directly to the "Kaisertal / Sparchen" trailhead in under ten minutes. Regional VVT buses service Ebbs, Niederndorf, and Durchholzen. Motorists travel via the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Kufstein-Nord) and leave vehicles at the large pay parking grounds at Kaisertal Sparchen or the ski lift base in Durchholzen.

Tips

Carry a headlamp or pocket flashlight to safely inspect the vast limestone interior of Tischofer Cave and imagine Ice Age hunters seeking shelter here millenia ago. Stop at the historic Veitenhof or Pfandlhof guesthouses in the Kaisertal to savor artisanal Tyrolean cheese dumplings and fragrant stone-pine schnapps.
saison: Mai bis Oktober (Kaisertal-Hauptweg auch im Winter geräumt)
